title: Severe-allergy bar never appears when opening a patient fresh
simple: On the general-clinic patient page, a bar listing severe allergies is supposed to stick to the top of the screen once the header scrolls away. It is set up while the page is still loading, before the header exists, and never sets itself up again. So on a normal first open of a patient it never shows, however far you scroll. It only works if the patient was already loaded.
example: Dr Hana opens Abebe (allergic to Penicillin) from the queue and scrolls down to the prescription section. The red allergy reminder that should be pinned at the top is missing, so the allergy is only visible if she scrolls back up.
why: A safety reminder that staff expect to see is quietly missing, so they may prescribe without the allergy in view. Dental clinics use a different patient screen and are not affected.
fix: Set up the pinned bar after the patient's details have loaded, so it works on the first open as well.

title: Last night's vital signs are shown as if taken today
simple: The 'last vitals' card is meant to warn 'not from today' when the readings are old. It only checks whether they are more than 24 hours old, not whether they were taken on an earlier day.
example: Nurse Tigist records Abebe's blood pressure as 128/82 at 8 pm. At 9 am the next morning Dr Hana opens his record and sees 128/82 with no 'not from today' note, and assumes it was taken at this morning's triage.
why: A doctor can make a decision based on readings from the day before, thinking they are fresh.
fix: Compare calendar days (Addis time), not hours, so anything taken before today's midnight is marked 'not from today'.

title: Failed exam list shows 'No examination on record'
simple: If the examinations list fails to load (bad connection, server busy), the dental exam card says 'No examination on record' instead of saying it could not load.
example: On a weak connection Dr Selam opens Dawit's chart. The exam list fails to load and the card says 'No examination on record', so she thinks no one has examined him and starts a new exam, while last week's diagnosis is actually on file.
why: The dentist works without the previous diagnosis and may create a duplicate, contradicting exam.
fix: Show a clear 'could not load the examinations – retry' message when loading fails, separate from the real 'none yet' message.

title: Editing a patient wipes passport, address and emergency contact
simple: The 'Edit details' window only sends the nine fields it shows. The server replaces the whole record, so the passport number, address and emergency contact are wiped every time anyone saves an edit, even if they only changed the phone. If two people edit the same patient at once, the later save silently replaces the earlier one.
example: Hanna at reception updates Almaz's phone number to 0922 111 111 and presses Save. Her address 'Bole, Addis Ababa', passport EP1234567 and emergency contact 'Abebe 0911 222 333' are now blank. Months later Almaz has a reaction in the chair and there is no emergency contact.
why: Patient information is lost during a routine task, and nobody knows it happened.
fix: Two layers. The edit window now hands back the passport number, address and emergency contact exactly as it loaded them. The server also changes only the fields a request actually sends: a field left out keeps its stored value, a field sent empty is cleared.

log.note: Found as the P0 of the pre-production audit (AUD-01): 66 of 684 production patients had been edited after creation. Fixed at both layers; the old 'PUT is a full replace' contract test was rewritten. Earlier values, if lost, exist only in the nightly dumps (14 nights) and weekly dumps (8 weeks).

title: Patient edits, deletions and allergy removals leave no record
simple: When a patient is registered the system records who did it. But when someone changes a patient's name, phone or birth date, deletes a patient, or removes an allergy or condition, nothing is recorded: no name, no time, no 'before' value.
example: A 'Penicillin – severe' allergy disappears from Almaz's record. The owner checks the activity history to find out who removed it and when, and there is nothing there except her registration from last year.
why: Changes to medical and identity information cannot be traced, so mistakes or misuse cannot be found or corrected.
fix: Record every patient change (with old and new values), deletion, and allergy or condition removal: who, when and what. Consider letting only clinicians remove allergies.
decision: Should reception still be allowed to remove an allergy, or only a dentist or doctor (with a reason)?

title: Old-register import merges family members sharing one phone
simple: When an old patient register is imported, anyone whose phone number already exists is treated as the same person, even with a different name and age. In 'skip' mode the person is dropped as 'already on file'. In 'update' mode the existing patient is renamed to the new person.
example: Abebe Kebede (born 1970) is registered with the family phone 0915 151 515. The old register also lists his wife Almaz Tadesse, 25, on the same phone. The import reports Almaz as 'Already on file' and never creates her record. In update mode, Abebe's record would be renamed to Almaz.
why: Whole family members go missing, or one person's medical history ends up under another person's name.
fix: Count it as the same person only when phone AND name (or birth year) match. Report phone-only matches as 'possible family member' and never rename an existing patient from them.

title: An imported card number can block all new registrations
simple: New patients get automatic card numbers P000001, P000002 and so on. If an old register is imported with card numbers in the same format, the counter eventually reaches one that is already taken. Registration then fails, and because the failed attempt does not move the counter on, every later attempt fails the same way.
example: Cure Dental imports its old book, where Abebe already has card P000124. Months later the counter reaches 124. Hanna tries to register a new patient and gets 'card number taken'. She tries again, and it fails again, for everyone.
why: Reception cannot register any new patient until someone fixes the database by hand.
fix: When the automatic number is already taken, skip to the next free one. Also move the counter past any imported P-numbers.

title: Imported old history can have a future date
simple: The 'paste old history' tool accepts a visit dated in the future and saves it as a signed visit. Imported notes are also marked as signed by the person importing them, with nothing to show they were copied from an old record.
example: While copying Abebe's paper file, Hanna types 2027 instead of 2017. The record shows a signed visit dated next year, signed by Hanna, and that visit sits at the top of his history.
why: The patient's history becomes misleading: wrong order, and notes look like a clinician wrote them in the system.
fix: Refuse dates after today (Addis time) and label imported entries 'imported from old records by …'.

title: Import dry run misses card numbers that are already taken
simple: The 'check file' (dry run) step of the patient import says a row will import fine even when its card number already belongs to another patient. Only the real import then fails that row.
example: The dry run says all 200 rows of the old register are ready. During the real import, row 57 (card LEG-90, already used) fails, and Hanna has to fix and re-import it.
why: The trial run can't be fully trusted, which causes extra work.
fix: Check card numbers against existing patients during the dry run too.

title: A patient's first name can be blanked out by an edit
simple: Registration refuses a patient with no first name, but editing does not. Saving spaces as the first name stores an empty name.
example: Hanna accidentally clears Almaz's first name while editing and presses Save. The record now shows only her surname on lists, receipts and the queue.
why: Patients become hard to find and can be confused with each other.
fix: Apply the same 'first name required' check when editing as when registering.

title: Deleting a patient who doesn't exist reports success
simple: If the system is asked to delete a patient that doesn't exist (or was already deleted), it reports 'done' instead of 'not found'.
example: Two receptionists delete the same duplicate record a second apart. Both screens say it worked, which is harmless but hides that it was already gone.
why: Mostly cosmetic. It can hide mistakes when other software is connected.
fix: Answer 'not found' when nothing was deleted.

title: Removing an allergy that doesn't exist reports success
simple: Removing an allergy that isn't there (already removed, or a wrong link) reports success instead of 'not found'.
example: Dr Hana and Nurse Tigist both remove Almaz's duplicate 'Dust' allergy from two screens. Both are told it worked.
why: Mostly harmless, but it hides the case where the wrong item was targeted.
fix: Answer 'not found' when no allergy was removed.

title: Removing a condition that doesn't exist reports success
simple: Removing a medical condition that isn't there reports success instead of 'not found'.
example: Two people remove Abebe's old 'Hypertension' entry at the same time. Both are told it worked.
why: Mostly harmless. It can hide a wrong action.
fix: Answer 'not found' when no condition was removed.

title: File upload with storage switched off shows a server error
simple: If file storage isn't set up or is unavailable, trying to upload a patient document shows a general server error instead of a clear 'file storage is not available' message.
example: Storage is down for maintenance. Hanna tries to attach Almaz's referral letter and sees 'Something went wrong' with no hint why.
why: Staff can't tell a storage problem from a broken system, so they report the wrong problem.
fix: Return a clear 'file storage is off or unavailable' message, the way lab uploads already do.

title: Some invalid patient entries cause server errors, not messages
simple: A condition with an unknown status, a document with a type the system doesn't accept, or a guardian who isn't a real patient are all rejected by the database. Staff see a general server error instead of an explanation. Nothing wrong is saved.
example: A connected tool sends Abebe's asthma with status 'chronic' (the system only knows its own statuses). The screen shows 'Something went wrong' instead of 'unknown status'.
why: Confusing errors, but no data is damaged.
fix: Check these values first and give a clear message.

title: Certificate actions on missing records give confusing errors
simple: Issuing a medical certificate for a patient that doesn't exist gives a server error. Voiding a certificate that never existed says 'already void'. Both should say 'not found'.
example: A broken link sends Dr Hana to void certificate #123, which does not exist. She is told it is 'already void', so she thinks someone else voided it.
why: Misleading message. No data is harmed.
fix: Answer 'not found' in both cases.

title: Sick-leave certificate can be issued with no start date
simple: In the certificate window, clearing the 'Rest from' date still leaves 'Issue & print' working. A sick-leave certificate is issued and printed with no start date.
example: Dr Selam gives Dawit 3 days' rest after an extraction, clears the date to change it and presses Issue by mistake. A certificate saying '3 days rest' with no dates is printed and given to his employer.
why: An official medical document is incomplete. It can be rejected by an employer or misused.
fix: Disable 'Issue & print' until a start date is filled in.

title: An impossible age like 150 is silently dropped
simple: When registering by age, typing an impossible age (for example 150) is not refused. The birth date is silently left blank and the form moves on.
example: Hanna mistypes Abebe's age as 150 instead of 50. The patient is registered with no birth date and no warning, and age-based dosing has nothing to go on.
why: Patients end up with no age, and the desk is never told.
fix: Show 'that age is not possible' and stay on the first step.

title: A future birth date can be saved when editing a patient
simple: The edit window accepts a birth date in the future and saves it.
example: Hanna enters Almaz's birth date as 15 Jan next year instead of last century. The record saves, and her age shows as blank or nonsense.
why: Wrong ages on the record and on certificates.
fix: Refuse birth dates after today.

title: Edit window accepts an invalid email that registration rejects
simple: Registration refuses an invalid email like 'not-an-email'. The edit window sends it without checking.
example: Hanna types Abebe's email without the @ and saves. It is stored, and any email to him fails.
why: Messages to the patient fail, and the two ways of entering an email disagree.
fix: Use the same email check in the edit window as at registration.

title: Old-history date defaults to yesterday just after midnight
simple: On the 'import old history' page, the record date defaults to today and cannot be later than today. 'Today' is worked out on world (UTC) time, so between midnight and 3 am Addis time it is yesterday.
example: Working late at 00:20 on 3 October, Hanna opens the import page. The date shows 2 October and she cannot choose the 3rd.
why: Small wrong date, but only for imports done after midnight.
fix: Use the Addis date for the default and the limit.

title: Import error list gives wrong row numbers after a blank line
simple: The failed-rows list from a bulk import promises each row's line number in the original sheet. Blank lines are removed before counting, so every row after a blank line is reported one line too early.
example: The report says 'row 5: name missing'. Hanna opens the spreadsheet at line 5, finds it blank, and has to hunt for Selam's row, which is really on line 6.
why: Time wasted, and the wrong row may get 'fixed'.
fix: Count lines before removing blank ones, so the numbers match the sheet.

title: Patient's age is a year short on their birthday morning
simple: The banner on the general-clinic patient page works out age on world (UTC) time. From midnight to 3 am Addis time on the birthday, it still shows last year's age. Other screens get it right, so the screens disagree.
example: At 00:20 on 3 October, the night nurse opens Almaz, who turns 26 that day. The banner says 25y.
why: Small, but an age can matter for dosing and it disagrees with other screens.
fix: Use the same calendar age calculation as the rest of the app.

title: A medical condition that fails to save shows no error
simple: When adding a condition (for example Asthma) fails, the window just stays open with no message. The allergy window does show an error; this one doesn't.
example: Dr Hana adds 'Asthma' for Abebe on a bad connection and presses Save. Nothing happens. She assumes it is slow, closes the window, and the condition was never saved.
why: An important condition can be missing from the record while the doctor believes it was saved.
fix: Show an error message when saving a condition fails.

title: Failed billing list says 'No charges yet'
simple: On the general-clinic patient page, if the billing list fails to load, it says 'No charges yet.' instead of 'could not load'.
example: The connection drops as Meron, the cashier, opens Abebe's page. It says 'No charges yet', so she lets him leave without paying the 600 birr he owes.
why: Staff think a patient owes nothing when they do.
fix: Show 'could not load the charges – retry' when loading fails.

title: Failed visit history says 'No recorded visits yet'
simple: If a patient's visit history fails to load, the page says 'No recorded visits yet.' instead of 'could not load'.
example: Dr Hana opens Almaz, who has been treated three times. The history fails to load and says 'No recorded visits yet', so she treats her as a new patient.
why: Doctors can miss previous diagnoses and treatments.
fix: Show a 'could not load' message with a retry button.

title: Failed lab history says no test was ever ordered
simple: If the patient's lab history fails to load, the panel says 'No tests have ever been ordered for this patient.'
example: Dr Hana checks whether Abebe's blood sugar was tested last month. The panel fails to load, says no tests ever, and she orders a repeat test he pays for again.
why: Duplicate tests and extra cost to the patient, or missed results.
fix: Show 'could not load' when the request fails.

title: Failed SMS log says nothing was sent to the patient
simple: The patient's message history says 'Nothing has been sent to this patient.' when it fails to load, the same as when nothing was really sent.
example: Almaz says she never got her reminder. Hanna opens her messages, the list fails to load and says nothing was sent, so the clinic decides SMS is broken when it isn't.
why: Wrong conclusions about whether patients were reminded.
fix: Show 'could not load the messages' when the request fails.

title: Failed appointment list says 'Nothing booked'
simple: On a patient's schedule page, if appointments fail to load, it says 'Nothing booked' and 'No upcoming visits'.
example: Abebe calls to ask when his next visit is. The page fails to load and says nothing is booked, so Hanna books him again, and now he has two bookings.
why: Double bookings and wrong information given to patients.
fix: Show 'could not load' instead of the empty message when loading fails.

title: Duplicate patients can still slip in at registration
simple: The 'is this patient already registered?' check runs separately from the save, so two desks registering the same person at the same moment both pass. Phone numbers typed at registration aren't standardised (0911… and +251911… look different), and there is no duplicate rule for patients without a birth date.
example: Abebe is registered as 0911 223 344 last year. Today he is registered again as +251 911 223 344 with no birth date. No duplicate warning appears and he now has two cards.
why: Split medical histories and split debts for one person.
fix: Standardise phone numbers before comparing, run the check inside the save, and match name plus phone when there is no birth date.

title: Deleted patients still show in queue and appointment lists; no merge tool
simple: When a patient is deleted, their queue entries and appointments still appear on the queue and appointment lists. There is also no way to merge two records for the same person, so deleting one is the only way to clean up a duplicate.
example: Hanna deletes Almaz's duplicate record, but 'Almaz' is still waiting on the queue board and booked for Thursday. Clicking her opens a record that no longer exists.
why: Confusing lists, and duplicates can only be fixed by deleting, which loses history.
fix: Hide deleted patients' entries from queue and appointment lists, and add a 'merge these two patients' tool with its own permission.

title: Dental exams can be overwritten or deleted with no copy kept
simple: A dental examination (complaint, findings, diagnosis, plan) can be edited by any dentist, and the old text is replaced with no earlier version kept. It can also be permanently deleted. The history record of the deletion doesn't even say which exam it was. The card keeps showing the original author after someone else edits it.
example: Dr Selam diagnoses 'irreversible pulpitis' for Dawit. Three weeks later a colleague 'tidies' the exam and changes the diagnosis, or deletes it. When Dawit complains about his treatment, nobody can show what the original diagnosis said.
why: The clinical record can be changed or erased without a trace, which is a medico-legal risk and makes mistakes impossible to investigate.
fix: Keep deleted exams hidden but recoverable (with who, when and why), save the previous version on every edit, and record who last changed it. Possibly lock exams after the day and allow additions only.
decision: After the clinic day ends, should an exam be locked so changes can only be added as dated notes, or stay editable with every version kept?

title: Deleting an X-ray destroys the file with no record
simple: When an X-ray or photo is deleted, the record is hidden and the image file itself is permanently deleted from storage. Nothing records who deleted it or why.
example: A new assistant cleaning up 'blurry' images deletes Dawit's pre-treatment X-ray. Months later, in a dispute about the root canal, the clinic has no X-ray and no record of who removed it.
why: Clinical evidence is lost for good and cannot be traced.
fix: Keep the file (or move it to a holding area deleted after 30–90 days), record who deleted it and why, and need a senior permission to delete anything older than today.

log.note: Half fixed (audit AUD-02): deleting an image or attachment now hides the record and KEEPS the stored file, so a mistaken delete is recoverable. Still open: who deleted it and why is not recorded, and files are not yet backed up (OPS-3). A retention rule that purges kept files after a set time is still to be built.

title: New clinic's first chart save is refused until conditions are opened
simple: A new dental clinic's list of tooth conditions (decayed, filled, missing…) is only created the first time someone opens that list. If a chart save arrives before that (another device, a page that loads the chart first), it is refused with 'unknown condition decayed'.
example: A newly set-up clinic's dentist marks UR1 as decayed on a tablet whose palette hasn't loaded yet, and gets 'unknown condition'. Opening the condition list once makes it work.
why: Confusing first-day error. The normal screen loads the list first, so it is rare.
fix: Create the default conditions when the clinic is set up (or the first time they are needed for a save).

title: A treatment plan can be renamed to a blank title
simple: Creating a treatment plan requires a name, but editing it doesn't. A plan can be saved with an empty title.
example: Dr Selam edits Dawit's 'Root canal' plan, clears the name and saves. Receipts and lists now show a nameless treatment.
why: Confusing receipts and lists.
fix: Require a name when editing, the same as when creating.

title: Image limit on the plan can be bypassed
simple: The subscription plan limits how many images a patient can have (for example 8). The limit is checked when an upload is prepared, but not when the image is finally recorded, so a 9th can get in by reusing an upload.
example: On the basic plan, a 9th X-ray for Dawit is accepted when a staff member re-sends an earlier upload.
why: The plan limit isn't enforced. It is a small leak in what the clinic pays for, not a patient risk.
fix: Check the limit again when the image is recorded.

title: Badly typed dates on dental reports cause server errors
simple: The dental calendar and 'unbilled treatment' report crash with a server error if a date in the link isn't in the expected format, instead of saying 'invalid date'.
example: The owner edits the report link by hand to 13/10/2026 and gets 'Something went wrong'.
why: Confusing error. Normal screen use sends correct dates.
fix: Check the date format and give a clear message.

title: Visit numbers differ between screens
simple: The same dental visit can be 'visit 2' on the visit card, 'visit 3' on the receipt and follow-ups list, and '4/4' versus '3 of 3' elsewhere. Screens count visits in different ways (by date, by original order, including cancelled ones). This also covers UX-2.
example: Dawit's visit 3 is moved earlier than visit 2. The visit card calls it visit 2, the receipt says 'Visit 3 of 4', and the follow-ups list says 'Rebook visit 3'. Dawit asks which visit he actually paid for.
why: Staff and patients get confused about what was done and paid, which leads to disputes.
fix: Use one numbering rule everywhere (calendar order, ignoring cancelled visits) and one total.

title: Follow-ups list numbers moved visits differently from the patient card
simple: The follow-ups list shows each visit's original number, while the patient card numbers visits in date order. A visit moved earlier is 'visit 2' on the card and 'visit 3' in follow-ups. This is part of DEN-5.
example: Hanna sees 'Rebook visit 3' for Almaz in follow-ups, opens her card, and finds the missed visit called 'visit 2'.
why: Confusion when rebooking.
fix: Number visits the same way as the patient card (fixed together with DEN-5).

title: Fast taps on the tooth chart can undo a colleague's change
simple: When the chart is tapped quickly several times, the screen can send an out-of-date version of some teeth and undo a tooth another dentist just changed. The server merges correctly. The problem is what the screen sends.
example: Dr Selam marks LL6 as filled while Dr Yonas, on another screen, quickly taps through several teeth. Dr Yonas's save sends the old LL6 value and Dr Selam's change disappears.
why: The chart can quietly show the wrong state of a tooth.
fix: Send only the teeth that were actually changed on this screen.

title: Tooth chart is basic: no surfaces, no children's teeth, no history
simple: The chart has 32 adult teeth in Palmer notation, one condition per tooth, no tooth surfaces, no baby teeth and no history view. Recording a procedure in a visit does not update the chart.
example: Dr Selam treats a 7-year-old and cannot chart baby teeth. For Dawit she can't mark 'mesial caries on LL6', only 'decayed', and after she fills it the chart still says decayed until she changes it by hand.
why: Not a bug, but a limitation. Clinics should know before using it for children or detailed charting.
fix: Plan a fuller chart: surfaces, children's teeth, several conditions per tooth, history, and procedures that update the chart.
decision: Is the fuller chart (surfaces, children's teeth) needed for current clinics, or can it wait? Tell clinics about the limit until then.

title: Visit notes can be edited by any dentist forever
simple: Treatment notes on a recorded visit stay editable by any dentist with no time limit, and the latest save wins. Earlier versions are only in the activity log.
example: Months after Dawit's extraction, a colleague edits the visit note, removing 'patient warned of numbness'. The note now reads differently from what was written on the day.
why: Clinical notes can be quietly rewritten after the fact.
fix: Lock notes after the clinic day and allow dated additions, or at least show 'edited by … on …'.
decision: Should visit notes lock at the end of the day (additions only), or stay editable with a visible edit history?

title: Small gaps in dental rules, reachable only by direct API calls
simple: A few dental rules are checked on screen but not on the server: changing a cancelled treatment's visits, reverting a visit with a zero fee, and repricing a cancelled visit. Normal screen use doesn't hit them.
example: Only a connected tool or a technical user could, for example, change a visit on a cancelled treatment for Dawit.
why: Low risk. Rules should hold however they are reached.
fix: Add the same checks on the server.

title: Typed examination notes can be lost
simple: The dental examination form has no saved draft and no 'you have unsaved changes' warning. Cancel throws away what was typed without asking, and so does opening another exam's Edit. The visit form has all of these protections; the exam form has none.
example: Dr Selam types 10 minutes of findings for Dawit, then clicks Edit on last month's exam to check something. Her new exam is gone without warning. A page reload or sign-out does the same.
why: Clinical findings are lost and re-typed from memory, which risks mistakes.
fix: Reuse the visit form's draft-saving: keep a draft per patient, warn before leaving, and ask before Cancel discards typed text.

title: Treatment notes lock while the bill waits; unsaved notes can be lost
simple: While a visit's bill is waiting at the cashier, the treatment notes are locked. If the dentist sends the bill to the cashier while still writing, the unsaved part of the note is dropped.
example: Dr Selam sends Dawit to pay mid-note. Her last two sentences vanish, and she can't add them until Meron collects the payment.
why: Lost clinical notes and dentists waiting on the cashier.
fix: Save the note before sending to the cashier, and let notes stay editable while the bill waits.

title: The visit being recorded can switch under the dentist
simple: On the dental visit screen, the visit being recorded isn't fixed. If the patient's data refreshes (another visit is moved or paid), the screen can switch to a different visit.
example: While Dr Selam records visit 2 for Dawit, Meron takes payment for visit 3. The screen refreshes and Dr Selam's notes are now on visit 3.
why: Treatment recorded against the wrong visit.
fix: Keep the chosen visit fixed until the dentist finishes or changes it.

title: Dental prescription needs a treatment and a paid fee
simple: A dentist can only write a prescription while recording a visit on a treatment plan that is paid for (or agreed to be paid later). An emergency painkiller with no treatment plan has no path.
example: Almaz walks in at 5 pm with severe toothache and only needs a painkiller prescription. Dr Selam has to create a fake treatment plan and fee first.
why: Workarounds create false treatments and fees, or the prescription is handwritten outside the system and its allergy check.
fix: Allow a stand-alone prescription from the patient's page, still with the allergy check.
decision: Should dentists be able to prescribe without a treatment plan or a fee (for emergency visits)?

title: Reception's 'Expected today' leaves out dental treatment visits
simple: Reception's 'Expected' list only reads booked appointments. Dental treatment visits planned for today (from treatment plans) are not shown, although the home dashboard counts them. At Cure Dental most arrivals are treatment visits.
example: The dashboard says five patients are still to come. Reception's list says 'Nobody booked today'. Dawit arrives for his root-canal visit 2 and is received as a walk-in, so his queue card isn't linked to the visit. If the dentist forgets to mark the visit done, he shows tomorrow as 'missed' although he came.
why: Reception can't prepare, treatment visits get wrongly flagged as missed, and screens contradict each other.
fix: Add today's planned treatment visits to 'Expected' (using the same rule as the dashboard), and link the visit when the patient checks in.

log.note: Explained in plain language; owner said go. Built: reception's Expected list now also shows a patient whose treatment course has a planned visit today (one row per patient, lowest visit number, tagged 'Treatment visit' with 'Root canal · visit 1 of 2', no clock because nothing was booked). A patient who is also booked appears once, as the booking; a patient already received leaves Expected and appears under Waiting; another branch's visits and finished or cancelled plans are left out. Receiving one goes through the walk-in door, which is correct because no appointment exists.
Full run green: server 755/0 (94 known), screens 1,872, journeys 15/15, routes 277/277, all coverage minimums held. Committed; deploying.

Deployed to app.clinicos.cc (commit 89ad722, pre-deploy backup taken, API ready, no errors in the log). No migration. Live check: no clinic has a visit planned for today or tomorrow yet, so nothing shows until a plan with a visit today exists. Waiting for the owner to verify.

title: SMS reminders can show the old date after a reschedule
simple: Each visit gets one reminder slot. If the visit is moved after a reminder is queued, the patient still gets the old date and never a reminder for the new date. The sender also doesn't re-check whether the patient has opted out or the visit was cancelled before sending.
example: At 10:00 Hanna moves Almaz's visit from tomorrow to next Tuesday. At 18:00 Almaz gets 'Your visit is tomorrow' and comes in for nothing. A patient who replied STOP at noon still gets the 18:00 text.
why: Patients come on the wrong day, miss the real visit, and opt-outs are ignored. This matters once SMS goes live (it is a test account today).
fix: Include the date in the reminder's identity, and just before sending check that the visit still exists with that date and the patient hasn't opted out. Skip with a reason otherwise.

title: Check-in can revive a cancelled booking or queue a patient twice
simple: Checking in a booking doesn't look at its status or whether it was already checked in. A cancelled appointment can be checked in, and pressing check-in twice (or two desks at once) creates two queue cards.
example: Hanna and Meron both check Almaz in at the same moment, and she appears twice on Dr Selam's queue. Dawit's appointment, cancelled yesterday, is checked in by mistake and comes back to life.
why: Duplicate queue cards, confused dentists, possible double fees.
fix: Refuse check-in of cancelled or completed bookings, and make a repeat check-in return the existing queue card.

title: Appointment status can jump anywhere, even from completed back
simple: Any appointment status can be changed to any other: a completed appointment can go back to 'confirmed'. Rescheduling moves an appointment whatever its status and skips the booking checks. Clashes show as server errors. Cancelling a checked-in appointment leaves its queue card in place.
example: Hanna accidentally sets Abebe's completed visit back to 'confirmed'. It reappears as upcoming, and reports now count one fewer completed visit.
why: Appointment history and counts become unreliable.
fix: Allow only sensible moves (for example booked → confirmed → checked in → completed, or → cancelled / no-show), and show clashes as a clear message.
decision: Should a completed or cancelled appointment ever be reopened (for example by a manager to correct a mistake), or never?

title: Patients booked with a departed dentist wait for nobody
simple: If the dentist a patient was booked with has been deactivated, check-in still puts the patient in that dentist's queue. Nobody sees them there.
example: Dr Yonas leaves and the owner deactivates him. Almaz arrives for her booking with him, is checked in, and waits an hour on a queue no dentist looks at.
why: Patients wait without being seen.
fix: At check-in, refuse with 'Dr Yonas is no longer active – choose another dentist', or put them in the department queue unassigned.
decision: When a booked dentist has left, should check-in stop and ask the desk to pick another dentist, or send the patient to the general department queue?

title: 'Missed visit' means different things on different screens
simple: Four screens decide 'missed' differently: the home dashboard looks back 7 days, the notification bell 14, the follow-ups list 30 (and counts finished treatments), and the visit card all time. The same patient is missed on one screen and not on another.
example: Dawit missed his visit 10 days ago. The bell tells the owner about it, the dashboard doesn't count him, and follow-ups lists him under 'Missed'. The owner can't tell which number is right.
why: Contradicting numbers, so missed patients get forgotten.
fix: Use one 'missed visit' rule everywhere.
decision: How far back should 'missed visit' look everywhere: 7, 14 or 30 days, or until the patient is rebooked or the treatment is closed? And should finished treatments ever count?

title: Follow-ups 'Missed' forgets visits older than 30 days
simple: The follow-ups list only looks back 30 days, so patients who abandoned their treatment more than a month ago drop off 'Missed' and nobody calls them.
example: Almaz stopped coming after visit 2 of 5 in July. By September she is no longer in 'Missed' and nobody contacts her.
why: Abandoned treatments, unpaid balances and lost patients go unnoticed.
fix: Keep a missed visit listed until it is rebooked or the treatment is closed (decided together with APT-8).

title: Midnight-to-3am times use world time, not Addis
simple: The queue board starts its day at 3 am Addis (midnight world time), so anyone arriving between midnight and 3 am isn't on today's board. The booking window also shows an appointment between midnight and 3 am on the day before, and saving it without changes moves it a day earlier.
example: An emergency patient arrives at 00:30 and isn't on the queue board. Hanna opens a 01:30 appointment for 5 October, presses Save without changing anything, and it moves to 4 October.
why: Rare for a day clinic, but a saved booking can silently move to the wrong day.
fix: Use the Addis day for the queue board's default and the Addis date in the booking window.

log.note: Owner question added from the night-hours test findings.

Decided (owner delegated the choice): a patient still waiting counts on today's waiting alerts whatever time they arrived. The alert describes who is in the waiting room now; someone waiting since 23:00 is the most urgent, not hidden. To be built when APT-9 is fixed, with a test that queues a patient at 23:00 Addis yesterday.

title: After a fee is paid, the queue card loses its booking link
simple: When a fee must be paid before a patient joins the queue, the queue card created after payment isn't linked to their appointment, and the live queue board isn't updated after payment.
example: Almaz pays at the cashier. Her queue card appears without her booking details, and Dr Selam's board doesn't show her until it is refreshed.
why: Patients wait unnoticed, and the appointment and the visit don't connect.
fix: Keep the appointment link through payment and notify the board when the patient is released.

title: Some lists don't hide deleted records
simple: A few appointment and queue lists don't filter out deleted records, so deleted items can still show up.
example: A deleted appointment for Abebe still shows in one list.
why: Small confusion.
fix: Add the missing 'not deleted' filters.

title: Yesterday's queue cards never close; dental visits have no time or chair
simple: Queue cards left open at the end of a day stay open forever. Dental treatment visits have only a date, no time or chair, so they can't be scheduled into slots.
example: Abebe's queue card from Monday is still 'waiting' on Friday. Three treatment visits are all 'today' with no times.
why: Clutter and no real chair scheduling for dental.
fix: Close stale queue cards automatically at the end of the day, and add an optional time and chair to dental visits.
decision: Do dental visits need a time and chair (real chair scheduling), or is date-only enough for now?

title: A finished queue visit can be moved back to waiting
simple: A queue card marked 'done' can be moved back to 'waiting'. The system checks only that the new state is a real state, not whether the move makes sense.
example: By mistake Hanna moves Almaz's finished visit back to 'waiting'. Almaz reappears on the dentist's board as if she has not been seen, with her finish time still set.
why: Confused queues and wrong waiting-time numbers.
fix: Allow only forward moves (waiting → in progress → done, or → left), and refuse reopening, or limit it to managers.

title: Setting priority on a queue card that doesn't exist reports success
simple: Setting the priority of a queue card that doesn't exist says 'done' instead of 'not found'.
example: A screen that hasn't refreshed raises the priority of a card already removed. It says it worked.
why: Cosmetic. It can hide a stale screen.
fix: Answer 'not found' when nothing was changed.

title: Queue patients can be assigned to the cashier or a stranger
simple: A waiting patient can be assigned to any user: the cashier, or even a user from another clinic. No patient data leaks to the other clinic (checked), but the patient is now 'with' someone who will never see them.
example: Hanna picks the wrong name and assigns Almaz to Meron the cashier. Almaz disappears from the dentists' lists and waits.
why: Patients get lost in the queue.
fix: Accept only active clinicians of this clinic when assigning.

title: A queue that fails to load says 'No patients'
simple: If the queue fails to load, the page says 'No patients in this range.', so an outage looks like an empty waiting room.
example: The server hiccups at 10 am. Dr Selam's queue page says no patients while three are waiting outside.
why: Patients wait unseen while staff think nobody is there.
fix: Show 'could not load the queue – retry' on failure.

title: Reassign window remembers the doctor picked last time
simple: The 'Reassign doctor' window keeps the doctor chosen the last time, even if that was cancelled, when opened for another appointment. One click can send a pointless 'reassign to the same doctor'.
example: Hanna picks Dr Abebe for Almaz, then cancels. She opens Reassign for Chaltu, who is already with Dr Abebe, and 'Reassign' is ready to press with Dr Abebe still selected.
why: Small risk of moving the wrong patient.
fix: Start the window empty each time it opens.

title: Reception 'New' and 'Register them' open the list, not the form
simple: Reception's 'New' button and the 'Register them' link go to the patients list with a 'new' marker the list ignores. The desk lands on the list, not the registration form, and the name they typed in search is lost.
example: Hanna searches 'Genet', finds nobody and clicks 'Register them'. She lands on the patient list and has to click 'New patient' and type Genet again.
why: Extra clicks at a busy desk.
fix: Link straight to the registration form (and carry the typed name over).

log.note: Fixed with the reception empty screens: 'New' and the no-match 'Register' now open /patients/new, and the typed name pre-fills the form (REG-FE-RECEP-035/036, REG-FE-PREG-040/041). Full run green.

title: Reminder hours box can't be cleared, so 48 becomes 148
simple: In the automatic-message settings, the hours and repeat boxes turn an empty value into 1 on every keystroke. Deleting '72' and typing '48' leaves '148'.
example: The owner changes the unpaid-bill reminder from 72 to 48 hours after the bill. It saves as 148 hours, so patients are reminded 6 days later instead of 2.
why: Reminders go out at the wrong time without anyone noticing.
fix: Let the box be empty while typing, and check the number only on Save.

title: Failed unread count says 'You're all caught up'
simple: If the unread-notification count fails to load, the notifications page counts it as zero and says 'You're all caught up', even above a list of unread notices.
example: The count request fails. The owner sees 'You're all caught up' and doesn't read the two missed-visit notices below it.
why: Important notices are ignored.
fix: Show no all-clear when the count failed (or work it out from the list).

title: Notice times say 'yesterday' based on hours, not the calendar
simple: A notification's age reads 'yesterday' when it is 24 to 48 hours old, whatever the calendar day. A notice from early this morning reads 'yesterday' late at night, and one from two days ago can read 'yesterday'. The page heading groups by calendar day, so the two disagree.
example: At 23:50 the owner sees a notice from 00:10 the same day labelled 'yesterday' under the 'Today' heading.
why: Small confusion about when something happened.
fix: Decide 'yesterday' by calendar day.

title: No 'you are offline' signal; chart says saved when it wasn't
simple: The app has no offline warning and requests have no time limit. The tooth chart says 'Saved automatically' even when nothing reached the server.
example: The Wi-Fi drops while Dr Selam charts Dawit's teeth. The chart says 'Saved automatically', she closes it, and the changes are gone.
why: Staff believe work is saved when it isn't.
fix: Show an offline banner, add request time limits, and only say 'saved' after the server confirms.

log.note: Explained in plain language; owner said go. Part of the description was already out of date: the tooth chart already showed '✓ Saved' only after the server confirmed (FEAT-CHART-1). The real gaps were a hung request (no time limit, so 'Saving…' for ever) and no warning anywhere. Built: every request gives up after 30 s (2 min for the Ministry push, bulk imports and the AI; 2 min for files sent to storage); a save with no answer says 'may not have been saved, check before doing it again'; a request that cannot be sent says 'could not reach the server' instead of a raw 'Failed to fetch'; a banner under the top bar says 'No connection to the server' or 'The server is slow to answer' and clears by itself (the browser's offline signal plus failed requests, then the server's /healthz is asked every 8 s until it answers). The tooth chart no longer says 'changes undone' after a timeout, because the save may have landed: it says 'Not confirmed — reload to check what was saved'.

Committed; deploying.

Waiting for the owner to verify: switch the browser to Offline (F12 → Network) or turn Wi-Fi off, and the banner must appear; turn it back and it must clear within about 8 seconds.

title: Patient page reloads 12 things every 6 seconds while a bill waits
simple: While a visit's bill is waiting at the cashier, the patient page re-fetches 12 sets of data every 6 seconds.
example: Dr Selam leaves Dawit's page open while he pays. The page keeps hammering the server, which slows things for everyone on a weak connection.
why: Slowness and data use, worse on weak connections.
fix: Check only the bill's status, less often, and refresh the rest once when it is paid.

title: After an update, an old tab can crash the whole app
simple: The app has one error screen for everything. After a new version is deployed, a tab that was already open may try to load a piece that no longer exists (the dashboard chart, for example), and the whole app, including the side menu, is replaced by the error screen.
example: After a lunchtime update, the owner clicks Home in a tab opened in the morning. The entire screen becomes 'This page could not be displayed', with no menu to go anywhere else.
why: Staff get stuck and may lose unsaved work when they reload.
fix: Add error catchers around each page and the chart, and reload automatically once when a missing piece is detected after an update.

log.note: Owner hit it live (TakingsChart chunk missing after an update). Fixed first: a missing piece after an update now reloads the tab once (at most once a minute) and fetches the new version; the dashboard chart is loaded through the same recovery; the server answers a missing /assets file with a plain 404 that is never cached, so a stale tab cannot be fed the page's HTML as if it were code.
Deployed to app.clinicos.cc (commit a67d218). Waiting for the owner to verify.

title: Cancelled confirm-dialog actions cause hidden errors
simple: When an action confirmed in a pop-up fails, the pop-up correctly stays open, but the error is also thrown again in the background as an unhandled error. Users see nothing extra. It clutters error logs and makes it hard to write a test for it (recorded as NEW-CONFIRM-1).
example: Removing an allergen fails. The dialog stays open with a message (fine), and the browser logs an extra 'unhandled error'.
why: Noise that can hide real errors in monitoring.
fix: Catch the error inside the confirm dialog after showing it.

title: 'No permission' errors are shown as connection problems
simple: When a page can't load because the user's role isn't allowed to see it, the message says to check the connection and retry, the same as a network failure.
example: Hanna opens the staff list, which her role can't see. She is told to check the connection and retries five times, then calls the owner about 'the internet'.
why: Wasted time and wrong support calls.
fix: Say 'you don't have access to this – ask the owner' when the server refuses for permission.

title: Crash screen falsely promises nothing was lost
simple: When a screen crashes, the error page says 'Your data is safe – nothing was saved or changed'. It can't know that: a save may have just gone through, or typed text may be gone.
example: Dr Selam's page crashes right after she pressed Save on an exam. The message says nothing was saved, so she types it again and creates a duplicate.
why: Staff are told not to check, which leads to duplicates or missing records.
fix: Change the message to 'Something went wrong. Check whether your last change was saved before trying again.'

title: Quick search (Ctrl+K) hides patients the server found
simple: The quick-search box (Ctrl+K / Cmd+K) asks the server for matching patients, then filters the results again by matching the typed letters against the patient's internal ID instead of the name. Most real matches are hidden and it says 'No results'.
example: Hanna presses Ctrl+K and types 'al' for Almaz Haile. The server finds her, but the box says 'No results', so Hanna decides she isn't registered.
why: The quickest way to find a patient doesn't work, which can lead to duplicate registrations.
fix: Turn off the second filtering for server results (or match on name and card number).

title: Dental clinic's Help Center talks about triage, which they lack
simple: A dental clinic has no triage step, but its Help Center tells reception to route patients to triage and says check-in sends them to triage.
example: A new receptionist at Cure Dental reads the help and looks for a triage screen that doesn't exist.
why: Confusing training material.
fix: Hide or reword triage text for clinics without triage.

title: Dental pages have no 'How this works' help button
simple: The Help Center promises a 'How this works' button on every page, but dental clinics' own pages (Chairside, Unbilled treatment) have none, and the Help Center doesn't list them.
example: A new dentist on the Chairside screen looks for the help button that the Help Center promised and finds nothing.
why: Less self-help for new staff.
fix: Write help entries for Chairside and Unbilled treatment.

title: Mixed words for the same thing across screens
simple: Different screens use different words for the same thing: treatment plan / course / treatment, session / visit, owes / owed / unbilled.
example: Hanna is told to 'bill the unbilled session' while her screen says 'visit owed'. She isn't sure it is the same thing.
why: Confusion and slower training.
fix: Pick one word for each idea and use it everywhere.

title: Treatment plan window overflows on small phones
simple: On a narrow phone (360 pixels wide), the new treatment plan window runs off the side of the screen.
example: Dr Selam creates a plan on her phone and can't see the right-hand edge of the visit amounts.
why: Harder to use on phones.
fix: Fix the window's layout for narrow screens.

title: Ethiopian date for years before 8 AD differs from the screen
simple: The server's Ethiopian-calendar conversion disagrees with the screen's by one day for dates before the year 8 AD (including an 'empty' date). Real dates (birth dates, visits) are converted correctly. This was checked for leap years and Pagumē.
example: Only an empty or corrupted date (year 0001) would show as -7-05-07 on a server document and -7-05-08 on screen. No real patient date is affected.
why: No real harm. It only matters if an empty date is ever printed, and that should show as blank anyway.
fix: Show empty dates as blank, and use the same rounding as the screen for very old years.
decision: Fix at all? Recommended: just make sure an empty date prints as blank, and leave ancient dates alone.

title: Unbilled list dates night visits to the day before
simple: The Unbilled treatment report works out each visit's date in world time (UTC), not Addis time. A visit given between midnight and 03:00 is dated the day before, counted as a day older, and left out when you filter for today.
example: Dr Selam finishes an emergency extraction at 00:40 on Sunday. On Sunday's Unbilled list it shows as treated Saturday, 1 day unbilled, and the 'today' filter does not show it at all, so the cashier misses it at closing.
why: Night work goes missing from 'today' and looks older than it is, so money owed is followed up late or not at all.
fix: Date every visit on the report by the clinic's Addis day, the same way the Finance page already does.

title: An old visit draft can come back after recording
simple: While a dentist types a visit record, the form saves a draft 0.8 seconds after typing. If the visit was saved before that timer fired, the save cleared the draft and then the timer wrote it back, so an old 'Draft restored' note could reappear later on a visit already recorded.
example: Dr Selam opens visit 2, the earlier draft is restored, and she presses Save straight away. Next week, reopening that visit shows 'Draft restored' with last week's text.
why: Confusing: it looks as if the record was not saved, and old text can be saved over the real record by mistake.
fix: When a visit is recorded, cancel any pending draft save before clearing the draft.

title: Registration fee charged on every visit, not once
simple: The system charges every 'Default' service on every day a patient arrives. A clinic whose rule is 'registration is paid once' is charging returning patients again, and patients brought over from the paper register pay as if new. There is no setting to choose once / every visit / again after N days.
example: At Joy Speciality, returning patients paid the 50-birr registration again 241 times (12,050 birr), mostly 8-30 days after their last visit. At Cure Dental, 13 of the 21 people who paid registration were already registered on paper.
why: Patients are overcharged against the clinic's own rule, and staff cannot explain the charge.
fix: A rule on each arrival service (every visit / once per patient / again every N days, optional renewal price), today's behaviour as the default, a reception preview that says why a fee is or is not charged, and the dead card-fee setting removed. Full design: docs/registration-fee-analysis.html.

fix: Oldest first, then by name, then by record id: the same order every time.

title: Tooth chart: marking takes many taps; no select-many or clear

example: Dr Yonas examines a new patient: 28 healthy, 2 decayed, 1 filled, 1 extracted. Today that is about 39 taps plus 32 pop-ups; a slip means going round the list again.
why: Slow at the chair, easy to mis-mark, and a clinical record that is hard to correct.
fix: Condition bar above the chart (pick a condition, then tap or drag teeth), select mode with quick selects, Clear for a tooth, a group or the whole chart, persistent Undo and Redo, clearer chart layout. Plan: docs/tooth-chart-plan.html.

title: Extras at the chair: no Send to cashier on the record form; no pay-before-continue

example: Dr Yonas adds an X-ray, 2,000 ETB, on the record form. It reads 'Owed now' with no button; the patient is not sent to pay and the doctor cannot tell later whether they did.
why: Unbilled extras are forgotten or billed after the patient has left.
fix: Send to cashier on every screen that shows extras; Not billed / At cashier / Paid stages with live status; Treat now, pay later with a reason; a gentle stop when finishing with an unpaid extra; quick-add chips and totals. Plan: docs/extras-at-the-chair-plan.html.

title: Printed documents: no clinic identity, logo, layout choice or preview
simple: Twelve things were printed (three receipts, Z-report, statement, two prescriptions, two lab papers, certificate, dental examination, pharmacy print), each with only the clinic name, no logo, tax number or layout choice; the pharmacy Print printed the whole web page and the lab report had no clinic identity.
example: A clinic with a printed letterhead and a TIN prints a receipt: it shows 'Abeba Dental Clinic' in monospace, no logo, no TIN, no duplicate marking on a reprint, and a refunded visit receipt reprints as a normal payment receipt.
why: Documents handed to patients, pharmacies, employers and tax officers look unofficial and cannot be checked; reprints cannot be told from originals.
fix: One print engine for every paper. Settings > Printing: logo (shape, size, position), English and Amharic names, address, phones, email, website, TIN, VAT, licence, three extra lines, a footer; header style (full, compact, name only, blank for your own letterhead), accent colour, typeface, text size; language and Ethiopian dates; per document: layout, paper (58 mm, 80 mm, A5, A4), which parts print, the clinic's own wording, and reworded labels. A live preview shows the clinic's own paper, and every print shows a preview first. A reprint of a receipt, prescription, lab request, lab report, certificate, Z-report or dispensing slip is marked DUPLICATE with who printed it first. Fixed on the way: a refunded visit receipt reprints as REFUNDED; the lab report carries the clinic identity and who collected and validated it; the pharmacy Print is a real dispensing slip; the statement lists where to pay.

title: The QR on a prescription proves nothing: no way to check a paper is genuine
simple: The QR on a printed prescription held a few lines of plain text. Scanning showed the text; nothing checked whether the prescription was real, cancelled, changed or already used, and anyone could print an identical QR.
example: Someone changes '7 days' to '70 days' on a paper, or photocopies a genuine one and takes it to two pharmacies. Both look exactly like the original and nobody can tell.
why: A pharmacy cannot trust a paper it cannot check, and a doctor cannot withdraw a prescription once it has left the building.
fix: The QR is now a link to the clinic's own record. Scanning opens a public page (no account) showing what the clinic issued: Genuine, Cancelled, A newer version exists, Past its validity, or Already dispensed, with the medicines, doctor, date and how many times it has been checked. A short code under the QR works when a camera will not. The doctor's name follows the printing switch. Plan: docs/paper-verification-plan.html.

title: The print preview can be left stuck on screen after printing

why: Staff are locked out of the screen after the most ordinary action they do all day.
fix: The preview now disappears completely before the paper goes to the printer, with no fade-out to wait for, and a double press of Print counts and prints once.

The clinic admin chooses Simple or Anatomical in Settings → Tooth chart.
example: A clinic switches to Anatomical. Dr Selam marks caries on 16's occlusal surface, a 2 mm gap in front of 11 and a rotated 12. The arches push apart at the gap and show '2mm'. If the clinic switches back to Simple, those findings are listed in words under the squares; nothing is lost.
